conventions.convention: The Hilbert pseudoinverse has domain R(K) ⊕ R(K)⊥ with the norm inherited from Y; it returns the minimum-norm preimage of the range component and annihilates the orthogonal component. Boundedness is not assumed.
The compact inverse model assumes neither injectivity, surjectivity nor closed range.

Inner products are linear in the first argument. Singular systems index exactly positive singular values: J = {1,…,r} at finite rank, J empty at rank zero, and J = {1,2,…} at infinite rank. Empty sums equal zero.
Countable Choice is explicit in the Hilbert pseudoinverse definition, closed-range theorem, Picard theorem and diagonal example.
The diagonal example uses coordinates n = 0,1,… and positive singular indices j = n+1, so s_j = 1/j and u_j = v_j = e_(j−1).

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For a bounded linear operator K between real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same field, the restriction of K to N(K)⊥ is a linear bijection onto R(K). Define D(K†) = R(K) ⊕ R(K)⊥ and K†(r+z) as the inverse restriction applied to r; this is the unique minimum-norm solution of Kx=r.

Assume Countable Choice. For the stated compact real or complex Hilbert-space map and complete positive singular system, Kx=y is solvable iff y ⊥ N(K*) and P_K(y)<∞. Moreover D(K†) = R(K) ⊕ R(K)⊥ = {y∈Y:P_K(y)<∞}, and K†y is the norm-convergent singular expansion with coefficients ⟨y,u_j⟩/s_j.

Let X,Y be real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same scalar field and K:X→Y compact linear. The inverse model has parameter space X, data space Y, admissible truth class X, and exact datum y=Kx†. Solving Kx=y asserts no injectivity, surjectivity or closed-range hypothesis.

Assume Countable Choice. For a compact linear operator K between real or complex Hilbert spaces, K† is bounded on D(K†), carrying the inherited data-space norm, iff R(K) is closed; these conditions are equivalent to R(K) being finite-dimensional.

seams_checked.note: The compact-model definition specializes the general forward-map interface to admissible class X and exact solution equation Kx=y without adding identifiability or stability.

Compact Hilbert-model references preserve the scalar fields and assumptions. Source elements are restricted to the kernel complement; minimum-norm claims do not assert recovery of arbitrary kernel components.
Uses the compact Hilbert forward-model interface. Regularized inverses and their additional assumptions are specified separately; no boundedness of the unregularized pseudoinverse is inferred.
The veto's F2 reproduces the pseudoinverse domain and minimum-norm action faithfully. Its continuity argument uses the inherited domain norm and retains Countable Choice.

F4 correctly states pseudoinverse action on exact range data. The reverse-order identity is justified only for the supplied common singular system and source datum; no general reverse-order law is attributed to the supplier.
The sequence model explicitly assumes infinite rank and Countable Choice, uses positive singular values and estimates parameters in N(K)⊥. Its one-based sequence indexing is explicit.
